chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said:

I prayed behind Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) for days, and it was so that whenever it was a prayer wherein is no loud recitation, he (peace be upon him) recited loudly with 'In the Name of Allah the Beneficent, the Merciful'; and he (peace be upon him) used to recite loudly during both the two Chapters.

key_terms.السُّورَتَيْنِ: The two Chapters (referring to Al-Fatiha and the following Surah)
key_terms.بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ: In the Name of Allah the Beneficent, the Merciful
key_terms.صَلَاةٌ لَا يُجْهَرُ فِيهَا: Prayer wherein is no loud recitation (silent prayer)

ai.seo_question: Did the Imam recite the Basmalah loudly in silent prayers?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the specific juristic practice of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding the audibility of the Basmalah and the two preceding surahs, distinguishing his method from general silent prayers. It serves as a key evidence in Shia fiqh for the ruling that the Basmalah is an integral part of Al-Fatiha and should be recited audibly in both quiet and loud prayers, reflecting the Imam's emphasis on complete recitation. This practice underscores the scholarly view that the Basmalah is not merely an introductory phrase but a verse of its own, warranting explicit vocalization.
